key_insight: A differentiable WMLES framework jointly learns subgrid-scale and wall closures end-to-end, showing that these closures must be optimized together because their effects are coupled through the resolved flow.
engineering_relevance: The method improves turbulence prediction, generalizes across Reynolds numbers, grids, and domains, and can reduce repeated CFD tuning costs by reusing trained closures after deployment.
method: Hybrid-Joint couples a differentiable flow solver with two composed neural operators for SGS and wall closures.
Each closure uses a trainable neural network plus a fixed differentiable layer that preserves the structure of the conventional closure form.
Training is driven by low-order statistics, with gradients back-propagated through the full solver to optimize both closures jointly.
evidence_signal: Across posteriori tests on a zero-pressure-gradient turbulent boundary layer (Re_   _  = 600--6500), the method outperforms WMLES baselines, extrapolates beyond the training range, and reproduces mean-velocity and energy-spectrum statistics.
watch_item: Because the approach relies on differentiable solver integration and joint optimization, implementation quality, numerical stability, and solver-specific differentiation can strongly affect performance and transferability.
paper_title: Differentiable Hybrid Neural-CFD Modelling of Wall-Bounded Turbulence: Coupled Learning of Subgrid-Scale and Wall Closures
